hardware.variant: Assembled ESP-Mosaico kit; CoreBoard and supplied BaseBoard revisions unconfirmed

inputs.name: Running vendor application; operator-reported screen labels
Host-side HTTP and WebSocket inspection on macOS arm64

scenario: After operator power-on and network setup, read the application root and the GET paths /api/status, /api/logs/status, /api/capabilities and /api/lua-modules. With Live Logs in WebUI enabled by the operator, connect to /ws/logs and observe for 10 seconds. Request paths were discovered in the served WebUI. No configuration, file, firmware or actuator write was performed.
expected: Settings HTML and JSON catalogs are readable; the enabled log endpoint accepts a WebSocket connection and sends a log frame.
observed: HTTP 200 and page title ESP-MOSAICO Settings. Log status enabled=true. WebSocket upgrade HTTP 101 succeeded and one informational http_logs frame arrived. Capability catalog returned 19 entries; Lua catalog returned 28 entries. The status response did not include hardware revision or firmware version. Host USB enumeration showed no Mosaico USB device or serial port during this observation.
limits: Pass applies only to the read-only vendor WebUI scenario, not EmberBSD boot or drivers.
Software and GSP labels were reported by the operator. They are not a measured firmware hash, ESP-Claw version or source commit.
CoreBoard and BaseBoard revisions remain unknown; the observation does not qualify either V1.0 or V1.2 wiring.
The single log frame confirms the subscription path, not sustained logging or capture of earlier boot messages.
Catalog enumeration does not test Lua execution, peripheral I/O, attached modules or model services.
USB data cable suitability and the firmware USB configuration were not isolated; absence of enumeration has no established cause.
Vibe Mode, ROM recovery, firmware updates, flash layout, Bluetooth, IEEE 802.15.4 and multi-board operation were not tested.
